info.title: ElonUz — Business API
info.description:
Student discounts platform — backend.

All endpoints are served under `/v1` and every response — success **and** error — uses the same envelope:

```jsonc
{ "success": true,  "status": 200, "code": null, "message": "OK",
  "result": <payload>, "error": null }

{ "success": false, "status": 404, "code": null, "message": "Biznes topilmadi",
  "result": null,
  "error": { "code": "BUSINESS_NOT_FOUND", "message": "Biznes topilmadi", "fields": {} } }
```

The HTTP status code and the `status` field are always equal. `message` is user-facing Uzbek
text. On 422 the per-field messages are in `error.fields`. Money is an integer number of
so'm (`currency: "UZS"`); dates are ISO-8601.

Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. On `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, refresh and retry.

The full OpenAPI JSON (feed this to the mobile client codegen) is at [/docs/business/json](/docs/business/json).

status.description: Always equal to the HTTP status code.

error.description: Null on success, filled on error.

required.description: The listing cannot be published unless this is filled in

multiple.description: True for MULTI_SELECT. The value is stored comma-separated: "S,M,L"

requiresCustomName.description: True for OTHER — `customCategoryName` then becomes required

Move the type to another catalog group (must exist in catalog_groups)

values.description: Present for SELECT / BOOLEAN / MULTI_SELECT / TAGS — only values that occur.

types.description: Narrows the group expansion. Every entry must belong to one of `groupKeys`.

saved.description: The wanted state, not a flip: `true` saves, `false` unsaves. Sending the same value twice is a no-op.

distanceMeters.description: Null when the request carried no coordinates.

matchedVia.description: Why this listing matched. Exact matches (CATEGORY) outrank ALL under RELEVANCE.

isDiscount.description: false for a plain single-price listing.

savedAmount.description: Null on a regular listing — never 0 as a placeholder.

nearestBranch.description: Null only for an online-only business.

bbox.description: Map viewport. In `mode: "MAP"` either this or `lat`+`lng` is mandatory.

openNow.description: Some branch is open right now, Tashkent time (UTC+5).

validAt.description: ISO-8601. The offer must also be valid at this instant; defaults to now.

endingWithinHours.description: Ends within this many hours — the "expires today" filter.

includeAllCategory.description: Whether `categoryKey = "ALL"` listings answer a category request.

includeCustomCategories.description: Whether listings with a free-text `customCategoryName` (categoryKey "OTHER") answer the request.

query.description: Prefix, word-boundary match over title, business, category and synonyms (§7).

by.description: RELEVANCE falls back to NEWEST when no `query` is sent.

direction.description: Defaults: DISTANCE / PRICE_* / ENDING_SOON ascending, the rest descending.

filter.description: Same shape as `POST /discounts/search`; `groupKeys`/`types` are optional here.

priceDelta.description: Amount added to the base price (may be negative)

promoCode.description: Returned to a signed-in student only; null for anyone else (D5).

remainingForUser.description: How many redemptions this student has left in the current period. Null when anonymous, or when the listing sets no per-user limit.

distanceMeters.description: Null when the request carried no coordinates.

tradeCenterFields.description: Empty when the branch is not inside a trade center.

matchedVia.description: Why this listing matched. Exact matches (CATEGORY) outrank ALL under RELEVANCE.

isDiscount.description: false for a plain single-price listing.

savedAmount.description: Null on a regular listing — never 0 as a placeholder.

nearestBranch.description: Null only for an online-only business.

images.description: Every image; the card carries only the cover.

branches.description: Every active branch, nearest first when coordinates were sent.

geo.description: Where the student is. Only fills in `distanceMeters` and orders `branches` nearest-first — it never hides a listing.

SuggestionKindDto.description: Which exact filter the client should send back when this row is tapped.

count.description: Visible listings this suggestion would yield. Never 0 — such a row is dropped.

query.description: What the user typed. Shorter than 2 characters returns an empty list rather than an error — the client asks on every keystroke.

groupKeys.description: Expanded to its business types. Required unless `types` is given (Q3).

types.description: Narrows the group expansion. Every entry must belong to one of `groupKeys`.

byAttribute.description: Attribute key → the values that actually occur, with counts.

priceLabel.description: Short label for the pin; rendered server-side.

isFavorite.description: Always false for an anonymous reader (D5).

lat.description: Centroid of the markers it holds.

maxDiscountPercent.description: Null when no listing in the cluster is discounted.

bounds.description: Extent of what is returned; null when the viewport holds nothing.

truncated.description: True whenever a marker was dropped or folded into a cluster.

zoom.description: Decides how coarsely markers are grouped when `clusterize` is on.

clusterize.description: Fold nearby markers into clusters once the viewport holds more than `maxMarkers`.

mode.description: LIST returns cards, COUNT the total plus facets, MAP one marker per branch in the viewport.

line.description: Line key (CHILONZOR | OZBEKISTON | YUNUSOBOD | HALQA) — group by this, not by name

regionId.description: Restrict the search to a region

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token — store securely; rotated on each refresh

otpCode.description:
The code from `POST /v1/auth/{student|business}/register/otp`.

**Required whenever `phoneNumber` is sent.** `phoneNumber` is unique, so a registration that claimed a number without proving it would lock out that number’s real owner for good — which is why there is no way to skip this.

Not needed for an email-only registration: phone is not required to create an account at all (email, Google and Apple are complete signups on their own), and verification is asked for later, at the actions where trust matters.

received.description: Part indexes stored so far, ascending. After an interruption, send the ones not listed here — in any order, in parallel, and repeats are harmless.

chunkSize.description: Bytes per part. Only the last part may be shorter.

totalBytes.description: The ceiling this session may not exceed — what you declared at `init`, or the server-side reserve when you opened a streaming session. Not a promise about your file’s final size.

conversationId.description: Required for the chat kinds; omit for PROFILE_PHOTO and STORY_*.

fileName.description: Original name, kept for FILE. Sanitised server-side.

totalBytes.description:
An **upper bound** on the finished file, used to reserve your daily quota and to bound the part index. It does not have to be exact.

If you know the size, send it. If you are still encoding, send something you are certain not to exceed — the source file’s size — and send the real figure to `complete`. Going over this bound is the one thing `complete` will refuse.

**Omit it entirely** to open a *streaming* session, for when the size is not knowable yet because encoding has not started. The session is charged against a server-side reserve, and `complete` then requires both `totalBytes` and `parts`. Quota is still checked here: a student with none left is refused at `init`, exactly as before.

The finished file’s real size. Send this when `init` was given an estimate — it is what the assembled parts are checked against. Omit it and the figure from `init` is used instead, which is what a client that knew the size all along should do.

parts.description:
How many parts the file was cut into — indexes `0 … parts-1`.

**Required for a streaming session** (one opened without `totalBytes`) and the field that marks the last part: with the size unknown up front, an unbroken run of parts that simply stopped early is indistinguishable from a finished upload, and the server would happily assemble a truncated video. Optional otherwise, and checked when sent.

DeviceTokenTypeDto.description:
Which channel this token belongs to (calls spec §7.3).

**Optional — today’s app sends nothing and should not start.** Omitted, it is inferred from `platform`: `IOS → APNS`, everything else `→ FCM`.

⚠️ Note the iOS default is `APNS`, not `FCM` as the spec’s table has it: this backend talks to Apple directly and an iPhone registers its raw APNs token, so `FCM` would mislabel it.

Send `APNS_VOIP` for the **PushKit** token, and send it as a **second** registration alongside the ordinary one — the same iPhone has two tokens and needs both rows. Replacing one with the other silently disables either messages or calls.

⛔ The `APNS_VOIP` channel carries calls and nothing else. It is not a faster push: iOS kills an app that receives one without immediately showing an incoming call, and repeated kills stop VoIP delivery to that device for good.

token.description: The device push token. `ANDROID`/`WEB`: the FCM registration token. `IOS`: the raw APNs device token — 64 lowercase hex characters; anything else is rejected with 422 `INVALID_DEVICE_TOKEN`. A PushKit token has the same shape.

type.description: One of `CHAT | LISTING | CONNECTION_REQUESTS | MY_LISTINGS | PROFILE` — as a string, not an enum, so an unrecognised value can be treated as "no destination" instead of breaking the response.

id.description: The id `type` addresses: `conversationId` for CHAT, `listingId` for LISTING. Null for the target types that name a screen (`CONNECTION_REQUESTS`, `MY_LISTINGS`, `PROFILE`).

type.description: One of `JOB | DISCOUNT | LISTING | CHAT | CONNECTION | SYSTEM` — a string, not an enum (see §1.1). Drives icon and colour only.

body.description: Optional — a row with no body is drawn as a title-only card.

target.description: Null when the row is informational and opens nothing.

readAt.description: When it was read, or null. ISO-8601 UTC.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC. Never a pre-rendered "2 hours ago" — that string would freeze at the moment it was written and still read "2 hours ago" the next day (§2.3).

unreadCount.description: Unread across the student’s **entire** history, not within `items` (§2.2). This is what the dot on the home screen shows, so it must not shrink just because the list was capped.

ids.description: The rows to mark, at most 200. Ids that are unknown, or belong to another student, are skipped silently rather than failing the batch (§3.3) — one stale id from the client’s cache must not cost the others their mark.

all.description: Marks every unread notification. Mutually exclusive with `ids`.

url.description: Requires the same bearer token as any other call.

photos.description: The student’s profile pictures, in display order — swipe through them on the profile screen. The first element always matches `avatarUrl`. **Empty** for a student who has never added one, in which case fall back to `avatarUrl` (which may itself be null).

bio.description: Short profile blurb, up to 140 characters. Never contains a link, a `@handle` or a phone number — those are rejected on write, so this is safe to render as plain text.

phoneNumber.description: E.164 phone number, subject to the target’s `phoneVisibility`: `EVERYONE` always, `CONNECTIONS` only once connected, `NOBODY` (**the default**) never. `null` when hidden — so expect `null` for most students, and do not draw the row at all when it is.

universityId.description: The value the student set on their own profile — the same string `GET /v1/students` accepts in `universityId`. There is no server-side university catalogue yet, so this is free-form (the app currently writes `emis-<profEmisId>`, e.g. `emis-142`).

online.description: Live presence. Real everywhere the viewer is allowed to see it — subject to the target’s `lastSeenVisibility`: `EVERYONE` always, `CONNECTIONS` (the default) only once connected, `NOBODY` never. When hidden this is `false` and `lastSeenAt` is `null`.

lastSeenAt.description: When the student last closed their last socket. `null` while online or hidden.

id.description: Catalogue id, or the provider’s own id.

packId.description: Our pack id. `null` for a sticker from search, which belongs to no pack of ours.

emoji.description: Catalogue stickers only; `null` for a sticker from search.

thumbUrl.description: Smaller preview, search results only. `null` for a catalogue sticker — a 512×512 WebP is already small enough to be its own preview, so fall back to `url`.

offset.description: Start of the selection in UTF-16 code units — the same units Kotlin/Swift count.

id.description: `null` once the original has been purged — there is nothing left to jump to.

senderName.description: Name to draw above the bubble — already resolved, do not look it up by id.

preview.description: Shortened original text (≤120). `null` for media — draw "📷 Rasm" and friends from `type`.

quote.description: The fragment the sender highlighted, or `null` for a plain reply.

originalDeleted.description: The original was deleted or purged after this reply was sent. Keep showing the quote — it is a snapshot — but drop the tap-to-jump affordance.

durationMs.description: Milliseconds of actual conversation; 0 when the call was never answered.

clientMsgId.description: Your own idempotency key, echoed back — set only when you are the sender, `null` for everyone else. Match your optimistic ("sending") copy against this rather than against the message text: two identical texts in a row are indistinguishable, and a media message has no text at all (§17.1).

deletedAt.description: When the sender deleted this message, `null` otherwise. The row keeps its `seq` and stays in the history — `body` is emptied and it no longer counts as unread. Render a "message deleted" placeholder (§18).

albumId.description: Shared by every image of one multi-image send — draw consecutive messages with the same value as a grid. Each is still its own message with its own `seq`.

attachment.description: Set for IMAGE, GIF, VIDEO, VOICE and FILE messages; null otherwise.

replyTo.description: Set when this message replies to another; null otherwise (§C2).

unreadCount.description: Messages from the other member with `seq > myReadSeq`.

myReadSeq.description: How far you have read (`ConversationMember.lastReadSeq`). The persisted counterpart of `unreadCount` — advanced by `POST /v1/conversations/{id}/read` or the `message:read` event.

peerReadSeq.description: How far the other member has read. Every message you sent with `seq <= peerReadSeq` is read (✓✓). Restores receipt state after a restart, when the live `message:read` event is gone.

peerDeliveredSeq.description: How far the other member’s device has received. `seq <= peerDeliveredSeq` is delivered (✓).

total.description: Unread messages across every conversation. Deleted messages are not counted.

conversations.description: How many conversations hold at least one unread message.

hasMore.description: More messages exist past this page, in the direction you are paging. Exact — the server reads one row beyond `size` rather than inferring it from the page length, so a last page that happens to fill exactly still reports `false` (§17.5).

text.description: Max 300 characters (422 `QUOTE_TOO_LONG`). Must be a real slice of the target’s body at `offset` — the server checks it and rejects a mismatch with 422 `QUOTE_NOT_FOUND`. It is stored as a snapshot, so an unchecked one would render forever as text the original never contained.

offset.description: Start of the selection in UTF-16 code units. Kotlin and Swift already count in these, so pass the index straight through — no conversion on either side.

url.description: Provider CDN url. Checked against a host allowlist.

replyToMessageId.description: Reply to this message. It must live in the same conversation (422 `REPLY_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`) and must not be deleted (422 `REPLY_TARGET_DELETED`).

quote.description: Quote a fragment of the target instead of the whole message. Never valid on its own — without `replyToMessageId` it is 422 `QUOTE_WITHOUT_REPLY`. Text messages only: media has no body to slice.

body.description: Required for `TEXT` (1–4000). An optional caption (≤1024) for `IMAGE`/`VIDEO`/`FILE`. Rejected for `GIF`/`VOICE`/`STICKER` — there is nowhere to render it.

mediaId.description: The id returned by `POST /v1/media/chat-upload`. Required for `IMAGE`, `VIDEO`, `VOICE`, `FILE` and an uploaded `GIF`. Single-use: an attachment belongs to one message.

gif.description: For a `GIF` taken from search. Use this **or** `mediaId` (an uploaded GIF), not both.

stickerId.description: For a `STICKER` from our own catalogue — an id from `GET /v1/stickers/packs`. Use this **or** `sticker`, never both (422 `STICKER_SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS`); a `STICKER` message needs exactly one of them.

sticker.description: For a `STICKER` taken from `GET /v1/stickers/search` — pass the search result back verbatim. Use this **or** `stickerId`, never both. The response renders both sources as the same `MessageDto.sticker`, so nothing downstream has to tell them apart.

albumId.description: Client-generated id shared by every image of one multi-image send (max 10). Each image is still its own message with its own `seq`; this only tells the client to draw them as a grid.

clientMsgId.description: Client-generated id — makes a retried send idempotent (C6)

clearedBeforeSeq.description: Everything with `seq <= clearedBeforeSeq` is gone for you. Drop it from the local cache; the server will never return it again. Messages sent after this keep climbing from here.

unreadCount.description: Always 0 — nothing is left to read.

DeleteScopeDto.description: `EVERYONE` deletes for both members and is allowed only on your own messages — anyone else’s land in `skipped` as `NOT_OWN`. `ME` hides the message on every device you own and leaves it untouched for the other member, so it works on any message in the conversation.

reason.description: `NOT_OWN` — someone else’s message under `EVERYONE`. `NOT_FOUND` — no such id. `NOT_MEMBER` — the id belongs to a conversation you are not in.

deleted.description: Ids actually deleted — or already deleted, which is the same result (idempotent).

lastMessage.description: The newest message still visible to **you**, or `null` if none is left. Under `scope=ME` the other member keeps seeing a different one — that is the feature working, not a bug.

ids.description: Message ids, 1–100, all from the same conversation (422 `MIXED_CONVERSATIONS` otherwise). Duplicates are collapsed. Ids that do not exist come back in `skipped` rather than failing the batch.

call.description: Null when there is no live call — close the CallKit session immediately.

peer.description: The other participant. Null only if their account has since disappeared.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the credential stays valid. Fetch a new one before placing a call once it has expired — the credential is not tied to a call and is not refreshed by one.
